newsitem.title: USA: Accused U.S. Unabomber faces two trials.
newsitem.headline: Accused U.S. Unabomber faces two trials.

text.p: Accused Unabomber Theodore Kaczynski will face two separate trials in California and New Jersey on charges stemming from a terrifying 17-year bombing spree, a federal judge ruled on Friday.
Kaczynski's lawyers had sought to have charges against him consolidated into one case in California, where he is accused of four attacks that killed two people and injured two others.

U.S. District Judge Dickinson Debevoise ruled that, because Kaczynski is also charged with the 1994 parcel bomb murder of a New Jersey advertising executive, he should also be tried in that state. Kaczynski has pleaded not guilty.

"While there may be a pattern to various bombings ..., each was a discrete and separate crime, terrible in nature, and there is no requirement that they all be tried together," the judge wrote in a 12-page ruling.

The New Jersey trial will follow a trial in Sacramento, California, scheduled to begin in November 1997. The judge estimated the first trial would take three to four months and the second trial would take three weeks.

Authorities say the 54-year old Kaczynski, a former university professor, largely targeted universities and airlines, earning him the "unabomber" nickname. He is being held without bail in Sacramento.
